text: They're saying {player} went into the Tumbled Watch alone and came out. Alone. I had it off a carter who had it off a Warden, so that's nearly first-hand.
You'll not have heard, because they'd not say it themselves: {player} carried bread to a door in {place} where nobody's carried anything in nine years. Three loaves. Three means something here.
Bar your door if {player}'s about. No, I'll not say what I heard. I'll say the dogs in {place} went quiet and they don't do that for nothing.
That one came up the Hushline Stair. Walked up. Nobody walks up. A Warden named them at the top step and hasn't slept right since, they say.
Merrick Gosling's got a verse about {player} now, and it's got to {place} already with two extra stanzas and a tune it was never written in.
The Toll's humming. Forty metres of cracked bronze in a hole in the ground and it's humming like a fly in a jug, and my grandfather said it did that once before and then wouldn't finish the sentence.
Pennywort's wheel turns with no water in the race. He's grinding with it and selling the flour and the flour keeps a month, and I've bought it, and so have you.

There was a lane off the Tamwick road that went up to a place with a hare cut on the well. Went to turn up it last month out of habit and there's no lane. Hedged right over. I sat in the cart a while.
The Boys are on the Larkbourne road again, keeping hall in the old Warden tower that's lying on its side. Nobody remembers the Larkbourne Boys, which is exactly what they're banking on.

Orchard men in {place} let the barrow-wights come up as far as the old yew and no further. Thing's got a bell grown into its heart and it hums, and a wight will stop dead at it and turn round. Nobody knows why and nobody's asking too loudly.
The buoy bells out on the Mere have been ringing on still nights. Still nights, mind. No swell. Four of us have heard it off {place} and we'd agreed not to make anything of it.
There's a hermit on Willow Isle who was a Tallymen clerk and stopped counting. He'll tell you the true price of anything you like, exactly, and then refuse to sell it to you.
There's a door under the city with no hinges that opens for names. Say your own if you're anybody. If you're nobody, say the name of whoever's wronged you; they say it finds that funny.
The Lamp's dimmer than it was. The keeper won't say so to a Sayer, because a Sayer would come and measure it, and we've all seen what their measuring does to a thing that was working.
The water in the Drowned Nave rises when there's singing in it. That's not a story; ask anyone from {place} who's rowed a Sayer out there and had to row them back faster.
The pool at Eelfathom runs a few seconds behind. You wave and it waves after. Lad from {place} sat there a whole afternoon trying to catch it up and came home very quiet.

The shaft at Oskeld sings when the wind's right, and the clans say there's a thing walking in it that's bone and rock and was people once. Half the Hold says it isn't a person. The other half won't say either way in front of children.
The Rope-Song's got seven verses and a hole where the eighth ought to be. Every memory-keeper for a thousand years has taken that breath and not one of them can tell you whose name goes in it.
The Briar's going grey in patches. Fourteen at midwinter, nineteen now, and the forester counts them every morning and has stopped telling people the number.

Out on the heath there's a fire that went out a hundred and seventy years ago with Greyfold's people still sat round it passing a cup. They'll not rise unless you touch the cup. They wave, though. They all wave.

The Choir's got twelve. There's a thirteenth lying face down a mile off as if it walked away, and it's got a head, and the head isn't the same as the others, and there's a Sayers' camp digging at it and arguing.

The Order's been keeping that ring a hundred and seventy-seven years waiting on somebody the door'll open for. It opens for the known, they say. Which means every one of them who kept faith with it and died grey at the ring was never going to be enough.
